text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Draft bill creating jobs for young people, a campaign pledge of the new Socialist-led government, to be presented to the cabinet on August 20. The plan may include renewable five-year contracts.
-- Consumer spending fell 2.9 percent in June.
-- Savings banks Caisses d'Epargne to negotiate with unions on retirement reform.
-- Pay TV company Canal Plus signs alliance with digital TV operators in Italy.
-- Thomson Multimedia posts 769 million franc loss for the first half of 1997, aims to break even by the end of the year.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Usinor loses out on bidding in privatisation of Spanish steel group CSI.
-- European Commission may approve recapitalisation of Thomson Multimedia in the next few days.
L'AGEFI
-- Societe Generale to restructure new subsidiary Credit du Nord and take over its asset management activities.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Sales of mobile phones soar in June.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin aims to create some 50,000 public sector jobs for young people before the end of the year.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Fast-food chain Burger King, a unit of Grand Metropolitan, to pull out of France because of low profitability.
-- German banks Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank eyeing acquisitions in France.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Burger King to quit France.
